overview: Two documents: a 1944 Moscow telegram on Japan's mobilization of merchant seamen up to age sixty, and a 1940 memo on Japan Times cartoons about U.S. rearmament and reluctance to sell Japan oil.

people.name: W. Averell Harriman
people.role: Sender of the telegram from Moscow; U.S. Ambassador to the Soviet Union

subfiles.title: Telegram from Harriman on the mobilization of Japanese merchant seamen
subfiles.about: Reports a Soviet news-agency account of extraordinary Japanese measures to mobilize merchant-fleet personnel.
subfiles.summary: Harriman relays a TASS report: Japan approved registering and mobilizing seamen up to age sixty, including those in other key jobs, and shortening merchant-marine student training.

subfiles.title: Department of State memorandum on Japan Times cartoons
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.about: Comments on three Japan Times cartoons transmitted with Tokyo despatch no. 4890 concerning the United States.
subfiles.summary: Memo describes three 1940 Japan Times cartoons judged favorable to U.S. interests, depicting American rearmament awakening and reluctance to sell oil to Japan.

interest: Shows wartime Japanese seamen mobilization and 1940 Japan Times cartoons on U.S. oil policy.
